name: NOCD
one_liner: Live video ERP therapy for OCD with a licensed therapist, plus an app with self-help tools and support groups; takes many insurance plans.

short_description: NOCD provides live video ERP therapy for OCD with licensed therapists, plus app tools and support groups; in network with many insurers or $120–$240.
long_description: NOCD is a US online therapy service that specialises in obsessive-compulsive disorder. You are matched with a licensed therapist in your state who is trained in exposure and response prevention (ERP) and meet by live video, with messaging, 24/7 self-help tools, a community and weekly support groups in the app between sessions. NOCD is in network with more than 40 insurers, including UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Cigna and many Blue Cross Blue Shield plans, and says most in-network members pay $50 or less per session; self-pay is $120 to $240 per session depending on length, with an interest-free $95-a-week payment plan. Published outcome data come from NOCD-funded observational studies of its own patients: in 3,552 adults, OCD symptom scores fell by an average of 43% over treatment, and a 2025 study reported similar results in children and adolescents. There is no randomized trial of NOCD. The website uses Meta and Google advertising cookies; therapy records are covered by HIPAA.
patient_summary: You book a free call with NOCD's care team, are matched with a licensed ERP-trained therapist in your state, and meet by video, with messaging and app tools between sessions. With in-network insurance most people pay $50 or less a session; self-pay is $120–$240 a session. Therapists do not prescribe medication.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance (most pay $50 or less); $120–$240/session self-pay
pricing.notes: Self-pay: $120 (30 min), $180 (45 min), $240 (60 min); interest-free payment plan at $95/week. In network with 40+ insurers including UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Cigna and many BCBS plans. App download is free.

privacy.notes: Therapy records are protected health information under HIPAA; NOCD says it does not sell data, but its website shares visitor activity with Meta and Google through cookies and pixels for advertising (not treatment data).

faqs.a: With in-network insurance most people pay $50 or less a session. Self-pay is $120 for 30 minutes, $180 for 45 minutes or $240 for 60 minutes, with an interest-free payment plan. Prices checked October 2026.
NOCD is in network with 40+ insurers, including UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Cigna and many Blue Cross Blue Shield plans. Check your own plan with NOCD before booking.

faqs.q: What kind of therapy does NOCD use?
faqs.a: Exposure and response prevention (ERP), the main evidence-based therapy for OCD, delivered by licensed therapists trained in it, by video, with messaging and app tools between sessions.
No. NOCD therapists do not prescribe. If you need medication for OCD, you would see a psychiatrist or your own doctor alongside therapy.
